title: ICAN Skills Level
issuer: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN)
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the ICAN Skills Level syllabus to the flagship's domain weightings. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A manufacturer buys a new production machine for N5,000,000 and pays N150,000 for installation and N200,000 for staff training. Under IAS 16, what amount should be capitalised as the cost of the machine?
options: N5,150,000, being the purchase price plus installation
N5,350,000, being the purchase price, installation and training
N4,800,000, being the purchase price less training
N5,000,000 only, being the purchase price
items.explanation: IAS 16 includes the purchase price and directly attributable costs of bringing the asset to the location and condition for its intended use, so installation of N150,000 is capitalised. Training is expensed, giving N5,000,000 + N150,000 = N5,150,000.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 16 Property, Plant and Equipment

items.stem: A delivery van costs N8,000,000, has an estimated residual value of N800,000 and a useful life of four years. Using the straight-line method, what is the annual depreciation charge?
items.explanation: Straight-line depreciation spreads cost less residual value over the useful life: (N8,000,000 - N800,000) / 4 = N7,200,000 / 4 = N1,800,000 each year.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 16 Property, Plant and Equipment

items.stem: An entity revalues a building for the first time from a carrying amount of N12,000,000 to a fair value of N15,000,000. Under IAS 16, how is the N3,000,000 increase treated?
options: Recognised only when the building is eventually sold
Credited to profit or loss for the year
Recognised in other comprehensive income and accumulated in a revaluation surplus
Debited to retained earnings
items.explanation: IAS 16.39 requires an increase on revaluation to be recognised in other comprehensive income and accumulated in equity as a revaluation surplus. It is transferred to retained earnings over time or on disposal, not taken to profit or loss.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 16 Property, Plant and Equipment

items.stem: Under IAS 16, which measurement models may an entity choose for a class of property, plant and equipment?
options: The recoverable amount model
The cost model only
The revaluation model only
Either the cost model or the revaluation model
items.explanation: IAS 16 permits a choice between the cost model and the revaluation model, applied consistently to a whole class of assets. There is no recoverable-amount model for property, plant and equipment; that concept belongs to impairment.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 16 Property, Plant and Equipment

items.stem: An airline replaces the engine of an aircraft at a cost of N40,000,000, which extends the aircraft operating life. Under IAS 16, how should the replacement cost be treated?
options: Capitalised as a separate component, with the carrying amount of the replaced part derecognised
Treated as inventory
Charged against the revaluation surplus
Expensed in full when incurred
items.explanation: IAS 16 requires the cost of a replacement part that meets the recognition criteria to be capitalised as a separate component and the carrying amount of the replaced part derecognised. Day-to-day servicing is expensed, but a major replacement is not.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 16 Property, Plant and Equipment

items.stem: Which statement about land and buildings is correct under IAS 16?
options: Both land and buildings are held at fair value and never depreciated
Land is normally not depreciated because it has an indefinite useful life
Land is depreciated over 50 years
Buildings are never depreciated
items.explanation: Land normally has an indefinite useful life and is therefore not depreciated, although it is tested for impairment. Buildings have a finite life and are depreciated, even when the revaluation model is applied.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 16 Property, Plant and Equipment

items.stem: At the start of year 3 an entity decides that a machine with a carrying amount of N6,000,000 will be used for a further three years rather than two. The residual value is nil. How is the change treated under IAS 8?
options: By ignoring the change until the asset is sold
As a prior-period adjustment restating opening retained earnings
Prospectively, by depreciating the carrying amount over the remaining three years
As an error correction in profit or loss
items.explanation: A change in the estimated useful life is a change in accounting estimate applied prospectively under IAS 8. The carrying amount of N6,000,000 is spread over the revised remaining life of three years, giving N2,000,000 a year.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 8 Accounting Policies, Estimates and Errors

items.stem: Under IAS 2, at what amount should inventories be measured?
options: At the higher of cost and net realisable value
At selling price less a normal profit margin
Always at cost
At the lower of cost and net realisable value
items.explanation: IAS 2.9 requires inventories to be measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value. This ensures assets are not carried above the amount expected to be recovered through sale.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 2 Inventories

items.stem: Inventory cost N50,000, can be sold for N56,000 and will incur selling costs of N8,000. At what amount should the inventory be carried under IAS 2?
items.explanation: Net realisable value is the estimated selling price less the costs to complete and sell: N56,000 - N8,000 = N48,000. Because NRV of N48,000 is below cost of N50,000, inventory is written down to N48,000.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 2 Inventories

items.stem: Which cost formula is NOT permitted for measuring inventory under IAS 2?
options: Weighted average cost
Last-in, first-out
Specific identification for unique items
First-in, first-out
items.explanation: IAS 2.25 prohibits the last-in, first-out method. FIFO, weighted average cost and specific identification are all permitted, with specific identification required for items that are not ordinarily interchangeable.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 2 Inventories

items.stem: Which of the following costs is excluded from the cost of inventory under IAS 2?
options: Transport costs to bring the goods to their present location
Purchase price of the goods
Abnormal amounts of wasted materials
Conversion costs directly related to production
items.explanation: IAS 2.16 excludes abnormal waste from the cost of inventory and expenses it. Purchase price, conversion costs and transport to the present location are all included in the cost of inventory.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 2 Inventories

items.stem: An entity wrote inventory down to net realisable value in year 1. In year 2 the reasons for the write-down no longer apply and the inventory is still on hand. What does IAS 2 require?
options: The write-down is reversed to the new selling price
The reversal is taken to other comprehensive income
The write-down must never be reversed
The write-down is reversed, but only up to the original cost
items.explanation: IAS 2.33 requires a reversal of a previous write-down when the circumstances change, limited to the amount of the original write-down so the new carrying amount does not exceed original cost. The reversal is recognised in profit or loss.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 2 Inventories

items.stem: At the reporting date an asset has a carrying amount of N150,000, a fair value less costs of disposal of N120,000 and a value in use of N135,000. Under IAS 36, what is the impairment loss?
options: Nnil
items.explanation: Recoverable amount is the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use, so N135,000. The impairment loss is carrying amount less recoverable amount: N150,000 - N135,000 = N15,000.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 36 Impairment of Assets

items.stem: Under IAS 36, which of the following is an internal indication that an asset may be impaired?
options: A significant adverse change in the technological, market or legal environment
The asset becoming obsolete or physically damaged
An increase in market interest rates
A fall in the asset market value greater than expected
items.explanation: IAS 36.12 lists obsolescence or physical damage as an internal indicator of possible impairment. A greater-than-expected fall in market value and adverse technological or market changes are external indicators.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 36 Impairment of Assets

items.stem: When an impairment loss is recognised for a cash-generating unit to which goodwill has been allocated, which asset must be reduced first?
options: Cash and actively traded financial assets
The largest asset in the unit
The goodwill allocated to the cash-generating unit
Land and buildings only
items.explanation: IAS 36.104 requires the impairment loss to be allocated first to reduce the carrying amount of any goodwill allocated to the cash-generating unit, then pro rata to the other assets, subject to each asset recoverable amount.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 36 Impairment of Assets

items.stem: Goodwill acquired in a business combination is impaired in year 2. In year 3 the circumstances that caused the impairment improve. Under IAS 36, which treatment applies?
options: The reversal is taken to other comprehensive income
The impairment of goodwill may be reversed
The impairment of goodwill is reversed only up to the original cost
The impairment of goodwill must not be reversed
items.explanation: IAS 36.124 prohibits the reversal of an impairment loss recognised for goodwill. Reversals are permitted for other assets where the estimates used to determine recoverable amount have changed, but never for goodwill.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 36 Impairment of Assets

items.stem: How many steps are there in the model for recognising revenue under IFRS 15?
options: Five
Six
Three
Four
items.explanation: IFRS 15 uses five steps: identify the contract, identify the performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate the price to the obligations, and recognise revenue when each obligation is satisfied.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers

items.stem: Under IFRS 15, revenue is recognised when an entity satisfies a performance obligation by transferring to the customer which of the following?
options: The legal title to the asset
Control of a promised good or service
The physical possession of the asset
An invoice for the promised good or service
items.explanation: IFRS 15.31 recognises revenue when control of the promised good or service transfers to the customer. Legal title and physical possession are indicators of control but not the test, and issuing an invoice is not sufficient.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers

items.stem: A contract bundles two products with stand-alone selling prices of N60,000 and N40,000 for a combined price of N90,000. Under IFRS 15, how much of the transaction price is allocated to the first product?
items.explanation: The price is allocated on the basis of relative stand-alone selling prices. Product 1 share = N60,000 / (N60,000 + N40,000) x N90,000 = 0.6 x N90,000 = N54,000.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers

items.stem: Under IFRS 15, variable consideration is included in the transaction price only to the extent that it is which of the following?
options: Expected to be received within one year
Recorded as a receivable in the accounting system
Approved by the customer in writing
Highly probable that there will not be a significant reversal when the uncertainty is resolved
items.explanation: IFRS 15.56 constrains variable consideration so that it is included only to the extent it is highly probable that a significant reversal will not occur when the uncertainty affecting it is resolved.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers

items.stem: An entity arranges for a third party to supply goods to a customer but controls the goods before transfer and bears inventory risk. Under IFRS 15, how should the entity recognise revenue?
options: As a principal, recognising the gross amount of consideration
As revenue net of cost of sales
Only when the third party confirms delivery
As an agent, recognising only the commission as revenue
items.explanation: Under IFRS 15 an entity that controls the goods before transfer acts as principal and recognises revenue in the gross amount of consideration. An agent, which does not control the goods, recognises only its commission.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers

items.stem: Under IFRS 16, how does a lessee initially account for a lease of property for five years?
options: As an operating lease with rentals expensed evenly
By recognising a right-of-use asset and a lease liability
By recognising only a disclosure of the commitment
By recording the full future rentals as an expense immediately
items.explanation: IFRS 16 removes the operating and finance lease distinction for lessees and requires recognition of a right-of-use asset and a corresponding lease liability, with depreciation and interest recognised over the term.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IFRS 16 Leases

items.stem: Under IFRS 16, the lease liability is initially measured at which amount?
options: The total rent payable over the first year
The undiscounted total of future lease payments
The present value of the lease payments that are not paid at the commencement date
The fair value of the underlying asset
items.explanation: IFRS 16.26 measures the lease liability at the present value of lease payments not paid at the commencement date, discounted using the interest rate implicit in the lease or the lessee incremental borrowing rate.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IFRS 16 Leases

items.stem: A lessee enters a lease with a total term of 10 months and elects the practical expedient. Under IFRS 16, how is the lease accounted for?
options: The asset is capitalised but no liability is recognised
The lease is treated as a finance lease
A right-of-use asset and lease liability are recognised
Lease payments are recognised as an expense on a straight-line basis
items.explanation: IFRS 16 permits a short-term lease exemption for leases of 12 months or less without a purchase option; the lessee then recognises the lease payments as an expense on a straight-line basis.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IFRS 16 Leases

items.stem: Which of the following qualifies for the low-value asset recognition exemption under IFRS 16?
options: A leased laptop of low value when new
A leased factory machine of N20,000,000
A fleet of leased delivery vans
A leased building with a value of N50,000,000
items.explanation: IFRS 16 permits the low-value exemption for assets that are low value when new, such as a laptop or small office equipment. Buildings, large machines and vehicle fleets do not qualify, and the assessment is on the asset, not the lease.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IFRS 16 Leases

items.stem: A lease requires three annual payments of N100,000 at the end of each year. The incremental borrowing rate is 10% and the three-year annuity factor at 10% is 2.4869. What is the initial lease liability, to the nearest naira?
items.explanation: The lease liability is the present value of the three payments: N100,000 x 2.4869 = N248,690. The undiscounted N300,000 overstates the liability because it ignores the time value of money.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IFRS 16 Leases

items.stem: Under IAS 37, a provision is recognised when there is a present obligation from a past event and which further condition is met?
options: The amount has already been paid
The obligation is certain to crystallise
It is probable that an outflow of resources will be required and the amount can be estimated reliably
The entity has signed a written contract
items.explanation: IAS 37.14 recognises a provision when a past event creates a present obligation, an outflow of resources is probable, and a reliable estimate can be made. A possible rather than probable outflow is only a contingent liability.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 37 Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets

items.stem: Which statement distinguishes a provision from a contingent liability under IAS 37?
options: A provision is only disclosed while a contingent liability is recognised
Both are recognised on the face of the statement of financial position
Neither is recognised in the financial statements
A provision is recognised in the financial statements while a contingent liability is not recognised but disclosed
items.explanation: A provision meets the recognition criteria and is recorded as a liability with a matching expense. A contingent liability is a possible obligation whose existence depends on uncertain future events, so it is disclosed unless the outflow is remote.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 37 Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets

items.stem: Under IAS 37, how is the amount of a provision measured?
options: At the best estimate of the expenditure required to settle the present obligation
At the amount a supplier would quote
At the amount already paid to advisers
At the maximum possible outflow
items.explanation: IAS 37.36 measures a provision at the best estimate of the expenditure required to settle the present obligation at the reporting date, using expected-value or most-likely-outcome methods as appropriate.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 37 Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets

items.stem: An entity has a contract to buy goods at above-market prices and the unavoidable costs of meeting the contract exceed the economic benefits. Under IAS 37 this is which of the following?
options: A contingent asset
An onerous contract for which a provision is recognised
A prepayment
Inventory to be written down only
items.explanation: IAS 37.66 defines an onerous contract as one in which the unavoidable costs of meeting the obligations exceed the economic benefits expected, and requires a provision for the present obligation.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 37 Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets

items.stem: In measuring a restructuring provision under IAS 37, which cost may be included?
options: Investments in new systems
Future operating losses expected after the restructuring
Direct expenditures necessarily entailed by the restructuring, such as employee termination benefits
Retraining and relocating continuing staff
items.explanation: IAS 37.80 allows only direct expenditures necessarily entailed by the restructuring, such as termination benefits, to be provided. Future operating losses and costs of retraining, relocating or marketing are not included.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - IAS 37 Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets

items.stem: A company pays rent of N20,000 a month. At 31 December the rent for December has not been paid or recorded. What adjusting entry is required?
options: Increase prepayments and reduce expenses by N20,000
Increase expenses and reduce payables by N20,000
No entry, because the rent will be paid next year
Increase expenses and increase accrued liabilities by N20,000
items.explanation: The December rent was incurred in the period, so an accrual is required: debit rent expense and credit accrued liabilities, increasing both by N20,000 and matching the cost to the period it relates to.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Accounting adjustments and the accruals concept

items.stem: An entity pays N120,000 on 1 October for 12 months of insurance. Its year end is 31 December. What is the prepayment at the year end?
items.explanation: Three months from October to December have expired, so 3/12 x N120,000 = N30,000 is expensed and the remaining 9/12 x N120,000 = N90,000 is carried as a prepayment at 31 December.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Accounting adjustments and prepayments

items.stem: A machine costing N12,000,000 with no residual value and a five-year life is acquired on 1 April. The entity depreciates assets from the month of acquisition. What is the depreciation charge for the year ended 31 December?
items.explanation: Annual depreciation is N12,000,000 / 5 = N2,400,000. From 1 April to 31 December is nine months, so the charge is N2,400,000 x 9/12 = N1,800,000.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Accounting adjustments and depreciation

items.stem: A company sold equipment with a cost of N5,000,000 and accumulated depreciation of N3,800,000 for N1,500,000 cash. What is the gain or loss on disposal?
options: Gain of N500,000
Loss of N1,200,000
Gain of N300,000
Loss of N300,000
items.explanation: Carrying amount is N5,000,000 - N3,800,000 = N1,200,000. Proceeds of N1,500,000 exceed the carrying amount, so the gain is N1,500,000 - N1,200,000 = N300,000.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Accounting for non-current asset disposals

items.stem: Interest income of N45,000 had been earned but not yet received or recorded at the year end. What adjustment is required?
options: Decrease income and increase a payable by N45,000
Increase income and increase a payable by N45,000
No adjustment is required until cash is received
Increase accrued income and increase income by N45,000
items.explanation: Income earned but not received is accrued: debit accrued income, a receivable, and credit income by N45,000, so that revenue is recognised in the period in which it was earned.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Accounting adjustments and accrued income

items.stem: Opening inventory was overstated by N200,000 and closing inventory is correct. What is the effect on reported profit?
options: Profit is understated by N200,000
Profit is overstated by N200,000
Profit is unaffected
Profit is overstated by N400,000
items.explanation: Profit is sales less opening inventory plus purchases less closing inventory. An overstatement of opening inventory increases cost of sales, so profit is understated by N200,000. Closing inventory is correct and has no further effect.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Preparation of financial statements and inventory

items.stem: Trade receivables are N2,000,000. The allowance for doubtful debts is to be increased from N80,000 to N120,000. What is the charge to profit or loss?
items.explanation: The movement in the allowance is charged to profit or loss: new allowance N120,000 less existing allowance N80,000 = N40,000. The closing allowance is not the expense; only the increase is.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Accounting adjustments and receivables

items.stem: At 31 December a company has a bank overdraft of N350,000 and a positive bank balance in another account of N120,000. Which is the correct presentation?
options: Show only the bank balance of N120,000
Offset and show a net overdraft of N230,000
Show N120,000 as an asset and N350,000 as a liability because there is no legal right of offset
Show only the overdraft of N350,000
items.explanation: Financial assets and liabilities are offset only where there is a legally enforceable right of offset and the intention to settle net. Without that right the bank balance and overdraft are presented separately.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Presentation of financial statements

items.stem: Under the Companies and Allied Matters Act, which body is primarily responsible for preparing the annual financial statements of a company?
options: The Nigerian Exchange Limited
The Corporate Affairs Commission
The external auditors
The directors
items.explanation: Directors are responsible for preparing financial statements that give a true and fair view and for maintaining adequate accounting records. Auditors report on those statements, and the regulator does not prepare them.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Companies and Allied Matters Act reporting

items.stem: Under the Companies and Allied Matters Act, a company's annual financial statements must be approved and signed by which persons?
options: Two directors
The company secretary only
All the shareholders at the annual general meeting
The auditor only
items.explanation: The Companies and Allied Matters Act requires the financial statements to be approved by the board and signed by two directors. The auditors report on the statements; they do not approve them.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Companies and Allied Matters Act reporting

items.stem: The auditors' report on a company's financial statements must state whether the statements do which of the following?
options: Have been prepared by the auditor
Give a true and fair view of the state of affairs and of the profit or loss
Contain no accounting errors at all
Have been approved by the shareholders
items.explanation: Auditors report whether the financial statements give a true and fair view and are prepared in accordance with the applicable reporting framework and the Companies and Allied Matters Act.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Statutory audit reporting

items.stem: Which of the following must be included in the directors' report accompanying a company's annual financial statements?
options: The detailed tax computation
The names of all customers
The proposed dividend and a review of the business
The audit work programme and materiality level
items.explanation: The directors' report reviews the state of the company affairs, the proposed dividend, principal activities and other matters required by the Companies and Allied Matters Act. Audit programmes, tax computations and customer lists are not part of it.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Directors' report under the Companies and Allied Matters Act

items.stem: At the start of an audit, what is the most appropriate first activity for the audit team?
options: Send confirmations to all customers before any planning
Issue the audit report with the agreed scope of work
Perform detailed tests of the closing inventory count only
Obtain an understanding of the entity and its environment, including internal control, to assess risk
items.explanation: ISA 315 requires auditors to understand the entity and its environment and identify risks of material misstatement before designing further procedures. Testing without planning would waste effort and may miss significant risks.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - ISA 315 Audit planning and risk assessment

items.stem: In audit planning, materiality is best described as which of the following?
options: The amount above which misstatements would influence the economic decisions of users
The audit fee agreed with the client
A fixed percentage of gross profit in every audit
The total value of all recorded transactions
items.explanation: Materiality reflects the amount by which information would influence users' decisions. There is no fixed percentage for every entity; the auditor applies professional judgement based on the size and nature of the entity.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - ISA 320 Materiality in planning and performing an audit

items.stem: Which source of audit evidence is generally the most reliable?
options: Management internal reports
A bank confirmation received directly by the auditor
A written representation from the finance director
Photocopies of purchase invoices held by the client
items.explanation: ISA 500 rates externally sourced evidence obtained directly by the auditor as more reliable than internally generated evidence or client-held photocopies. Management representations are used only where other evidence is unavailable.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - ISA 500 Audit evidence

items.stem: Auditors compare a client's sales and gross profit ratios with prior years and budgets. This type of evidence is which of the following?
options: A legal confirmation
A test of controls
An analytical procedure
A physical inspection
items.explanation: Comparing financial ratios and trends against expectations is an analytical procedure under ISA 520, used in planning, as substantive evidence and in the overall review of the financial statements.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - ISA 520 Analytical procedures

items.stem: Audit working papers should be retained because they do which of the following?
options: Are filed with the Corporate Affairs Commission
Show the client how to prepare the accounts
Replace the financial statements
Provide the record of the procedures performed, evidence obtained and conclusions reached
items.explanation: ISA 230 requires audit documentation that enables an experienced auditor to understand the procedures performed, the evidence obtained and the conclusions reached. Working papers support the auditor opinion and are not a public filing.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - ISA 230 Audit documentation

items.stem: Which internal control is most effective at preventing the concealment of cash theft in the receipts function?
options: Segregating the duties of handling cash, recording receipts and preparing the bank reconciliation
Increasing the number of cashiers on duty
Requiring cash to be kept in a locked drawer
Having the same employee receive cash, record it and prepare the bank reconciliation
items.explanation: Segregation of duties means no single person controls cash handling, recording and reconciliation, which reduces both fraud and error. Combining those duties in one employee is the weakness the control is designed to prevent.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Internal control and segregation of duties

items.stem: An organisation control environment is primarily influenced by which of the following?
options: The number of computers on the network
The tone at the top, including the ethical values and commitment of those charged with governance
The size of the internal audit budget
The choice of accounting software
items.explanation: The control environment is the foundation of internal control and reflects the governance and ethical tone set by management and the board. Tools, budgets and software support control, but the environment is driven by people at the top.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Internal control and the control environment

items.stem: During an audit the auditors identify a significant deficiency in internal control. To whom should it be communicated on a timely basis?
options: To no one until the audit report is issued
Only to the external auditors own staff
To management, and to those charged with governance when it is significant
To the general public immediately
items.explanation: ISA 265 requires significant deficiencies in internal control to be communicated in writing to those charged with governance in a timely manner. Deficiencies of lesser significance are usually reported to management.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - ISA 265 Communicating deficiencies in internal control

items.stem: An auditor concludes that a misstatement in the financial statements is material but not pervasive. Which opinion is appropriate?
options: An adverse opinion
A disclaimer of opinion
An unmodified opinion with no modification
A qualified opinion
items.explanation: ISA 705 requires a qualified opinion when misstatements are material but not pervasive to the financial statements. Adverse opinions are used for pervasive misstatements and disclaimers for pervasive scope limitations.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - ISA 705 Modifications to the opinion

items.stem: The auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence about a single material item, but the possible effects are confined to that item. Which opinion is appropriate?
options: A qualified opinion
An adverse opinion
An unmodified opinion
A disclaimer of opinion
items.explanation: A scope limitation that is material but not pervasive results in a qualified opinion. A disclaimer is used only where the possible effects of the inability to obtain evidence are pervasive and could affect many elements of the financial statements.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - ISA 705 Modifications to the opinion

items.stem: A chartered accountant has a substantial shareholding in a company she audits. This situation primarily threatens which fundamental principle?
options: Confidentiality
Objectivity, through a conflict of interest and self-interest
Professional behaviour
Professional competence and due care
items.explanation: A financial interest in an audit client creates a self-interest threat to objectivity because the accountant judgement could be influenced by personal gain. Independence safeguards or declining the engagement may be required.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Professional ethics and independence

items.stem: Which of the following best describes the fundamental principle of confidentiality for an accountant?
options: Confidentiality ends when the engagement is completed
Confidentiality applies only to tax clients
Information acquired through professional work must not be disclosed without proper authority, unless there is a legal or professional right or duty to disclose
All client information must be published in the financial statements
items.explanation: Confidentiality requires an accountant to refrain from disclosing information acquired through professional relationships without proper authority, and it continues after the relationship ends. Legal or professional duties to disclose are exceptions.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Professional ethics and confidentiality

items.stem: A Nigerian company with turnover of N500 million in its accounting year is a large company. What is the standard companies income tax rate applicable to its taxable profits?
items.explanation: Under the Companies Income Tax Act a large company with turnover above N100 million is taxed at the standard rate of 30% of taxable profits. The 0% rate applies only to small companies and 7.5% is the VAT rate.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Companies income tax rates

items.stem: A company has turnover of N80 million and is not excluded from the medium-company regime. Which companies income tax rate applies?
items.explanation: A medium-sized company with turnover between N25 million and N100 million is taxed at 20% of taxable profits. The 0% rate is for small companies and 30% is for large companies.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Companies income tax rates

items.stem: Which of the following companies qualifies for the small-company exemption from companies income tax?
options: A company with turnover of N60 million
A company with turnover of N25 million or less
A company with turnover of N200 million
A company in the banking sector with turnover of N20 million
items.explanation: A small company with turnover of N25 million or less is exempt from companies income tax, subject to statutory exclusions for certain sectors such as banking and insurance. Turnover of N60 million or N200 million makes it medium or large.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Small company exemption from companies income tax

items.stem: A company has no taxable profit after capital allowances but it does have gross turnover. Which minimum tax applies?
options: 3% of share capital
No tax is payable because there is no profit
0.5% of gross turnover
2% of gross turnover
items.explanation: Where a company has no taxable profit and meets the minimum tax conditions, the minimum tax is generally 0.5% of gross turnover. Minimum tax ensures a basic contribution even where capital allowances reduce taxable profit to nil.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Minimum tax under the Companies Income Tax Act

items.stem: For companies income tax purposes, a company assessable profit is computed from which of the following?
options: The audited turnover only
The directors dividend declarations
Cash received and paid during the year only
The accounting profit adjusted for allowable and disallowable items on the correct tax year basis
items.explanation: Assessable profit starts from the adjusted profit of the trade, after adding back disallowable expenses and deducting non-trade income, computed on the basis of the correct accounting period.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Computation of assessable profit

items.stem: For an expense to be deductible in computing adjusted profit, it must generally be which of the following?
options: Wholly, exclusively, necessarily and reasonably incurred for the purpose of the trade
Approved by the tax authority in advance
Paid in cash
Capital in nature
items.explanation: The Companies Income Tax Act deductibility test requires expenditure to be wholly, exclusively, necessarily and reasonably incurred in the production of the profits of the trade. Capital expenditure is dealt with through capital allowances rather than as a deduction.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Allowable and disallowable expenditure

items.stem: Which of the following expenses is NOT deductible in computing a company adjusted profit?
options: Employee salaries and wages
Fines and penalties for breach of the law
Rent for business premises
Interest on a business loan
items.explanation: Fines and penalties imposed for breach of the law are not incurred wholly, exclusively and necessarily for the trade and are disallowed. Salaries, business rent and loan interest incurred for the trade are deductible.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Allowable and disallowable expenditure

items.stem: How does the tax system treat depreciation charged in a company accounts?
options: Depreciation is deductible only for small companies
Depreciation is fully deductible
Depreciation is disallowed and replaced by capital allowances
Depreciation is deductible for buildings only
items.explanation: Accounting depreciation is not an allowable deduction for companies income tax; instead, capital allowances are granted on qualifying capital expenditure. Depreciation is therefore added back to accounting profit.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Capital allowances in lieu of depreciation

items.stem: A company incurs a trading loss. Under the Companies Income Tax Act the loss may generally be which of the following?
options: Offset against the personal income of the directors
Refunded in cash by the tax authority
Carried back indefinitely against past profits
Carried forward indefinitely and set against future profits of the same trade
items.explanation: Trading losses are carried forward and relieved against future assessable profits of the same trade, subject to the statutory rules, rather than being refunded or offset against directors income.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Loss relief under the Companies Income Tax Act

items.stem: At what rate is tertiary education tax charged on the assessable profit of a Nigerian company?
items.explanation: Tertiary education tax is charged at 3% of a company assessable profit and is collected for the education tax fund. The rate was increased from 2% to 3% by the Finance Act.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Tertiary education tax

items.stem: What is the standard rate of value added tax in Nigeria?
items.explanation: The standard VAT rate is 7.5%, increased from the former 5% by the Finance Act. VAT is a consumption tax borne by the final consumer.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Value added tax rate

items.stem: Under the value added tax regime, which statement about small companies is correct?
options: VAT applies only to imports
All companies must charge VAT regardless of turnover
A company with turnover of N25 million or less is not required to charge VAT
Small companies charge VAT at 2%
items.explanation: The VAT Modification Order exempts a supplier with turnover of N25 million or less from charging VAT, so small companies do not include VAT on their invoices. Larger suppliers must register and charge VAT.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Value added tax registration and small companies

items.stem: A company output VAT is N300,000 and its input VAT on allowable purchases is N120,000. What VAT is payable to the tax authority for the month?
items.explanation: VAT payable is output VAT less allowable input VAT: N300,000 - N120,000 = N180,000. Input VAT is recoverable only where the related goods or services are used for taxable supplies.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Value added tax output and input

items.stem: Input VAT incurred on purchases used to make exempt supplies is generally which of the following?
options: Not recoverable
Recoverable at half the rate
Recoverable only in the following year
Fully recoverable
items.explanation: Input VAT is recoverable only on purchases used to make taxable, including zero-rated, supplies. VAT on purchases used to make exempt supplies is not recoverable and forms part of the cost.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Value added tax recovery of input tax

items.stem: By what day of the following month must a VAT return and payment generally be filed?
options: The 10th day
The 21st day
The last day
The 30th day
items.explanation: VAT returns are filed monthly with payment on or before the 21st day of the month following the transaction month. Late filing attracts penalties and interest.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Value added tax returns and remittance

items.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes zero-rated from exempt supplies under value added tax?
options: Zero-rated supplies are outside the tax net entirely
Exempt supplies bear VAT at 5%
Zero-rated supplies are taxable at 0% and allow input VAT recovery, while exempt supplies bear no VAT and input VAT is not recoverable
Both allow full input VAT recovery
items.explanation: Zero-rated supplies are taxable at 0%, so related input VAT is recoverable. Exempt supplies are not taxable and related input VAT is not recoverable, making the distinction important for cost.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Value added tax zero-rated and exempt supplies

items.stem: On which transaction is value added tax charged in Nigeria?
options: The payment of personal income tax
The issue of a company share capital
The payment of dividends to shareholders
The supply of goods and services in Nigeria other than exempt and zero-rated items
items.explanation: VAT is charged on the supply of taxable goods and services in Nigeria. Personal income tax, share issues and dividend payments are not supplies for VAT purposes and are outside its scope.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Value added tax taxable supplies

items.stem: A trader sells goods for N200,000, and the selling price is stated to be exclusive of VAT. What is the VAT charged at the standard rate?
items.explanation: VAT is 7.5% of the value of the supply: N200,000 x 7.5% = N15,000. The customer pays N215,000, being the price plus the VAT.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Value added tax computation

items.stem: Under the Pay-As-You-Earn system, the employer is required to do which of the following?
options: Deduct tax only from directors fees
Deduct tax from employees salaries and remit it to the tax authority as an agent
Pay the employees tax out of company profits without deducting
Leave employees to file and pay their own tax monthly
items.explanation: PAYE makes the employer the collecting agent of the tax authority: it deducts tax from employees emoluments and remits it to the relevant tax authority. The employer may be liable for unremitted amounts.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Pay-As-You-Earn administration

items.stem: By what date must an employer generally remit PAYE deducted from employees salaries?
options: The last day of the same month
The 30th of June each year
The 10th day of the following month
The 21st day of the following month
items.explanation: PAYE deducted in a month must be remitted on or before the 10th day of the following month. The 21st day is the VAT deadline.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Pay-As-You-Earn remittance

items.stem: An employee earns gross income of N3,600,000 a year. The consolidated relief allowance is the higher of N200,000 or 1% of gross income, plus 20% of gross income. What is the allowance?
items.explanation: 1% of gross income is N36,000, which is less than N200,000, so the fixed N200,000 applies. Adding 20% of gross income of N720,000 gives N200,000 + N720,000 = N920,000.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Personal income tax consolidated relief allowance

items.stem: Under the graduated personal income tax bands, what rate applies to the first N300,000 of taxable income?
items.explanation: The first N300,000 of chargeable income is taxed at 7%. The rate rises through 11%, 15%, 19% and 21% for successive bands, reaching 24% on income above N3,200,000.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Personal income tax graduated rates

items.stem: For PAYE purposes, the tax authority with jurisdiction over an employee tax is generally determined by which of the following?
options: The employer place of business
The employee place of residence in the year of assessment
The employee job title
The bank used to pay the salary
items.explanation: Under the Pay-As-You-Earn regulations, tax is remitted to the tax authority of the state where the employee resides in the year of assessment. The employer location and job title do not determine jurisdiction.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Pay-As-You-Earn jurisdiction

items.stem: Which of the following best describes the personal income tax treatment of a partner share of partnership profit in Nigeria?
options: Only the senior partner is taxed on the whole profit
The partnership itself pays companies income tax on the profit
Each partner is taxed on their share of the profit in their own name
Partners pay no tax on partnership profit
items.explanation: A partnership is not a taxable entity for companies income tax; each partner is assessed on their share of the partnership profit under personal income tax. This reflects the separate legal status of partners.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Taxation of partnerships

items.stem: In computing taxable profits, capital allowances are granted on which basis?
options: Only for companies in the banking sector
Only where the asset is leased out
In addition to accounting depreciation
In lieu of accounting depreciation on qualifying capital expenditure
items.explanation: Capital allowances replace accounting depreciation for tax and are granted on qualifying capital expenditure incurred on assets used for the trade. Depreciation is disallowed and added back.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Capital allowances principles

items.stem: A company incurs N10,000,000 on qualifying plant and machinery. What is the initial allowance at the standard rate of 50%?
items.explanation: Initial allowance on plant and machinery is 50% of qualifying expenditure: N10,000,000 x 50% = N5,000,000 in the first year. The annual allowance applies afterwards.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Capital allowances on plant and machinery

items.stem: What is the standard annual allowance rate on plant and machinery for capital allowance purposes?
items.explanation: The annual allowance for plant and machinery is 25% of cost, claimed after the initial allowance until the expenditure is fully allowed. Industrial buildings use 10% and furniture 20%.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Capital allowances on plant and machinery

items.stem: A company spends N20,000,000 on an industrial building. What is the initial allowance at the standard rate of 15%?
items.explanation: Initial allowance on an industrial building is 15% of qualifying expenditure: N20,000,000 x 15% = N3,000,000. The annual allowance of 10% applies thereafter.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Capital allowances on industrial buildings

items.stem: What annual allowance rate applies to furniture and fittings for capital allowance purposes?
items.explanation: The annual allowance on furniture and fittings is 20% of cost. Industrial buildings attract 10% and plant and machinery 25%.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Capital allowances on furniture and fittings

items.stem: A company disposes of an asset whose tax written-down value is N2,000,000 for N2,800,000. What tax treatment applies to the N800,000 excess?
options: A balancing charge is added to profits
A balancing allowance is deducted from profits
The excess is ignored
The excess is treated as a capital allowance
items.explanation: Where disposal proceeds exceed the tax written-down value, the excess is a balancing charge added back to taxable profits. A shortfall would instead be a balancing allowance deducted from profits.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Balancing adjustments on disposal

items.stem: Investment allowance may be claimed in addition to capital allowances at what rate on qualifying plant and machinery?
items.explanation: An investment allowance of 10% of qualifying expenditure on plant and machinery may be claimed in addition to capital allowances for eligible activities such as industrial and agricultural production.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Investment allowance

items.stem: A company has taxable profit before capital allowances of N3,000,000 and available capital allowances of N2,000,000. What is the taxable profit after capital allowances?
items.explanation: Capital allowances reduce assessable profit: N3,000,000 - N2,000,000 = N1,000,000. Any capital allowance in excess of profit would be carried forward rather than create a cash refund.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Deduction of capital allowances

items.stem: Which of the following is an essential element of a valid contract?
options: Approval by a court of law
Registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission
A written document witnessed by a lawyer
Offer, acceptance, consideration and intention to create legal relations
items.explanation: A valid contract requires offer and acceptance, consideration, capacity, intention to create legal relations and legality of object. Writing is required only for certain contracts, and court or registry approval is not a general requirement.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Essentials of a valid contract

items.stem: A supermarket displays goods on its shelves with price tags. In contract law this display is generally which of the following?
options: An invitation to treat
An acceptance of the customer offer
A binding unilateral contract
An offer to sell at the tagged price
items.explanation: Displaying goods with a price is an invitation to treat, inviting customers to make an offer at the till. The customer offer may be accepted or refused, as illustrated in Fisher v Bell.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Offer and invitation to treat

items.stem: In contract law, consideration is best described as which of the following?
options: A promise to do something in the future only
Something of value given by each party as the price of the other promise
The written record of the agreement
A payment of money by the seller
items.explanation: Consideration is the price for which each party promise is bought, and it must have some value and not be past. It may be a promise or an act, not necessarily money.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Consideration in contract law

items.stem: An agent contracts with a third party on behalf of a disclosed principal. Who is generally liable on the contract?
options: Both the agent and the third party jointly
The agent personally
The principal
The third party only
items.explanation: Where an agent acts for a disclosed principal within the agent authority, the principal is bound and liable on the contract. The agent is not personally liable unless the agent exceeded authority or assumed liability.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Agency and the liability of the principal

items.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of a general partnership under Nigerian law?
options: A partnership is a separate legal person from its partners
Partnerships must always have at least 20 partners
Partners have limited liability for the firm debts
Partners have unlimited liability for the firm debts
items.explanation: In a general partnership, partners have unlimited liability for the debts of the firm, and the firm is not a separate legal person from the partners. Limited liability belongs to incorporated companies.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Law of partnership

items.stem: The principle that a registered company is a legal person separate from its members was established in which case?
options: Salomon v A Salomon and Co Ltd
Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co
Donoghue v Stevenson
Hyde v Wrench
items.explanation: Salomon v A Salomon and Co Ltd established that a company is a legal entity distinct from its shareholders, so members are generally not liable for the company debts beyond unpaid amounts on their shares.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Separate legal personality of a company

items.stem: Which of the following is a consequence of incorporation under the Companies and Allied Matters Act?
options: Directors cannot be employees of the company
The company has perpetual succession and can sue and be sued in its own name
Shareholders are personally liable for all company debts
The company must wind up whenever a shareholder dies
items.explanation: On incorporation a company gains separate legal personality, perpetual succession, and the capacity to sue and be sued in its own name. Members liability is generally limited to the amount unpaid on their shares.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Companies and Allied Matters Act incorporation

items.stem: Which of the following best describes the fiduciary duty of a company director?
options: To maximise the directors own remuneration
To disclose all company information publicly
To act in the best interests of the company and avoid conflicts of interest
To act in the best interests of the largest shareholder only
items.explanation: Directors owe fiduciary duties to the company to act in good faith in its best interests, exercise care and skill, and avoid conflicts of interest. They do not owe duties to one shareholder at the expense of the company.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Duties of company directors

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the five fundamental principles of the ICAN code of ethics?
options: Confidentiality
Integrity
Objectivity
Profitability
items.explanation: The fundamental principles are integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality, and professional behaviour. Profitability is a commercial objective, not an ethical principle.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Fundamental principles of professional ethics

items.stem: An accountant is offered a large gift by a supplier who is bidding for a client contract. Accepting it would most directly threaten which principle?
options: Objectivity and integrity
Confidentiality
Professional behaviour only
Professional competence and due care
items.explanation: A significant gift creates a self-interest threat that could bias professional judgement, threatening objectivity and integrity. The accountant should decline the gift or apply safeguards to remove the threat.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Threats to the fundamental principles

items.stem: Which statement best reflects the principle of integrity for a chartered accountant?
options: Accepting every engagement offered
Being straightforward and honest in all professional and business relationships
Maximising the client tax savings whatever the law says
Keeping all client information secret forever
items.explanation: Integrity requires being straightforward and honest, which means an accountant must not be associated with misleading information or unlawful conduct. Aggressive tax planning that breaks the law would breach integrity.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Integrity as a fundamental principle

items.stem: An accountant has prepared a client financial statements. The client asks the accountant not to disclose a material misstatement to the auditor. What should the accountant do?
options: Resign without taking any further action
Comply, because the client pays the fees
Refuse, because integrity and professional behaviour require not being associated with misleading information
Disclose the misstatement to the general public
items.explanation: Under the fundamental principles an accountant must not knowingly be associated with misleading information. The appropriate response is to refuse and consider reporting internally or withdrawing, not to comply with the request.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Professional behaviour and integrity

items.stem: Which of the following best describes professional competence and due care?
options: Guaranteeing that no errors will ever occur
Delegating all work to unqualified staff
Charging the highest fee the client will bear
Maintaining professional knowledge and skill at the required level and acting diligently in accordance with standards
items.explanation: Professional competence and due care require an accountant to keep up to date and to act diligently in line with technical and professional standards. It does not guarantee perfect work, but it demands reasonable care and current knowledge.
items.reference: ICAN Skills Level syllabus - Professional competence and due care
